svg.text: "Are you who you say you are?"
Grace logs in with her password and a one-time code.
The system is now sure she is Grace, of Nyati Cinemas.
This is the front door lock. It is necessary. It is not enough.
Grace is genuinely Grace. She now requests booking
✗ Must be refused — by a rule she cannot bypass
This is the wall between flats. Different problem, different tool.
The single most expensive mistake in multi-tenancy
Believing that because login works, tenants are separated. A logged-in user with a valid token who changes an ID in the URL is the classic breach.
Authentication happens once, at the edge. Isolation must be enforced on every single data access, by something lower than the
feature developer — a database policy, a scoped credential, a framework the developer cannot forget to call.
